blocks.text: 简要说明

inlines.text: 简要说明
你的 Claude 套餐有五小时限制和每周限制。OpenRouter API 密钥两者都没有。你改为按使用的 token 付费。
最快的配置方式是 Ori Harness：
ori claude
会在该会话中通过 OpenRouter 启动 Claude Code，使用浏览器登录，无需粘贴密钥。

claude-or
的 shell 函数中，这样
claude
仍然使用你的套餐。
从 Claude Sonnet 5.5 开始。一次典型的简短 Claude Code 会话在 Sonnet 5.5 上花费 $0.16，在 Opus 5.5 上花费 $0.31，在 Haiku 5.5 上花费不到一美分。
不要相信 Claude Code 打印出的费用。在我们的测试中，它显示某次运行花费 $0.375，而我们实际被收取 $0.008。请改为查看你的密钥或 Activity 页面。
当你的套餐重置后，再次输入
claude
。无需撤销任何操作。

blocks.text: 为什么 Claude Code 会触及使用额度限制？

inlines.text: 为什么 Claude Code 会触及使用额度限制？

blocks.text: Claude 套餐有两个同时生效的限制。第一个在你首次提示后五小时重置。第二个每七天重置一次。Anthropic 并未公布任一限制的确切提示次数。Claude Code 使用的 token 比普通聊天多得多，因此你可能会在任务进行到一半时用尽额度。此时，Claude Code 会停止并告诉你额度何时重置。Anthropic 关于使用额度的帮助文章解释了这两个限制。

inlines.text: 第 2 步：添加一个切换到你的密钥的命令

blocks.text: 你可以把这些变量加到 shell 配置文件里，但那样每次 Claude Code 会话都会消耗你的密钥。我们希望你的普通 claude 命令继续使用你的套餐，所以把这些变量放进一个小型 shell 函数里。把下面这段加到 ~/.zshrc 或 ~/.bashrc 中：

inlines.text: 你可以把这些变量加到 shell 配置文件里，但那样每次 Claude Code 会话都会消耗你的密钥。我们希望你的普通
claude
命令继续使用你的套餐，所以把这些变量放进一个小型 shell 函数里。把下面这段加到
~/.zshrc
或
~/.bashrc
中：

blocks.text:
claude-or() {
  ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="https://openrouter.ai/api" \
  ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="$OPENROUTER_API_KEY" \
  ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="" \
  ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL="anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5" \
  ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL="anthropic/claude-opus-5.5" \
  ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL="anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5" \
  CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL="anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5" \
  claude "$@"
}
前三行是关键：

inlines.text: 前三行是关键：
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL
让 Claude Code 把请求发送给我们。
ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN
存放你的 OpenRouter 密钥。
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
必须为空。如果不为空，Claude Code 可能会尝试登录 Anthropic。

blocks.text: 其余四行是可选的。它们告诉 Claude Code 为 Sonnet、Opus 和 Haiku 分别使用哪个 Claude 模型。它们还会把子代理——Claude Code 自行启动的较小辅助任务——发送到 Haiku 5.5。

blocks.text: 达到限额时我可以使用更便宜的模型吗？

blocks.text: Tl;dr

inlines.text: Tl;dr
Your Claude plan has a five-hour limit and a weekly limit. An OpenRouter API key has neither. You pay for the tokens you use instead.
The quickest setup is Ori Harness:
ori claude
starts Claude Code on OpenRouter for that session, with a browser sign-in and no key to paste.
To do it by hand, three environment variables point Claude Code at OpenRouter. We put them in a shell function called
claude-or
, so
claude
still uses your plan.
Start with Claude Sonnet 5.5. A typical short Claude Code session costs $0.16 on Sonnet 5.5, $0.31 on Opus 5.5, and less than one cent on Haiku 5.5.
Don’t trust the cost Claude Code prints. In our test, it showed $0.375 for a run we were billed $0.008 for. Check your key or the Activity page instead.
When your plan resets, type
claude
again. There is nothing to undo.

blocks.text: Why does Claude Code hit a usage limit?

inlines.text: Why does Claude Code hit a usage limit?

blocks.text: Claude plans have two limits that run at the same time. The first resets five hours after your first prompt. The second resets every seven days. Anthropic does not publish an exact number of prompts for either one. Claude Code uses many more tokens than a normal chat, so you can run out in the middle of a task. When that happens, Claude Code stops and tells you when your limit resets. Anthropic’s help article on usage limits explains both limits.

When that happens, Claude Code stops and tells you when your limit resets.
Anthropic’s help article on usage limits
explains both limits.

blocks.text: An OpenRouter API key does not work this way. You pay for each token you use, and you can keep going as long as you have credit.

blocks.text: Ori Harness starts the Claude Code already on your machine with OpenRouter settings in place. Install it and start Claude Code through it:

inlines.text: Ori Harness
starts the Claude Code already on your machine with OpenRouter settings in place. Install it and start Claude Code through it:

blocks.text:
curl -fsSL https://openrouter.ai/labs/ori/install.sh | bash
ori claude --model anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5

Ori opens a browser so you can sign in with your OpenRouter account. It uses OAuth, so there is no key to create or paste. Only sessions you start with ori claude run on OpenRouter, so plain claude keeps using your plan, and you switch back by typing claude when your plan resets. The usage goes on your OpenRouter bill. If you are in an organization, a guardrail with a budget limit on your account caps what it can spend, and OpenRouter applies it to Ori sessions too.

blocks.text: Step 2: Add a command that switches to your key

inlines.text: Step 2: Add a command that switches to your key

blocks.text: You could add the variables to your shell profile, but then every Claude Code session would charge your key. We want your normal claude command to keep using your plan, so we put the variables in a small shell function instead. Add this to ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc:

inlines.text: You could add the variables to your shell profile, but then every Claude Code session would charge your key. We want your normal
claude
command to keep using your plan, so we put the variables in a small shell function instead. Add this to
~/.zshrc
or
~/.bashrc

blocks.text:
claude-or() {
  ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="https://openrouter.ai/api" \
  ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="$OPENROUTER_API_KEY" \
  ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="" \
  ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL="anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5" \
  ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL="anthropic/claude-opus-5.5" \
  ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL="anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5" \
  CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL="anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5" \
  claude "$@"
}
The first three lines are the ones that matter:

inlines.text: The first three lines are the ones that matter:
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL
tells Claude Code to send its requests to us.
ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN
holds your OpenRouter key.
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
must be empty. If it is not, Claude Code may try to sign in to Anthropic instead.

blocks.text: The other four lines are optional. They tell Claude Code which Claude model to use for Sonnet, Opus, and Haiku. They also send sub-agents, the smaller helper tasks Claude Code starts on its own, to Haiku 5.5.

inlines.text: Frequently asked questions

blocks.text: Does OpenRouter have usage limits for Claude Code?

inlines.text: Does OpenRouter have usage limits for Claude Code?

blocks.text: There are no five-hour or weekly limits. The only limits are on spending: how much credit you have, the limit you set on your key, and any budget your team admin has set.

inlines.text: There are no five-hour or weekly limits. The only limits are on spending: how much credit you have, the limit you set on your key, and any budget your team admin has set.

blocks.text: Are the models the same as on my Claude plan?

inlines.text: Are the models the same as on my Claude plan?

blocks.text: Yes. They are Anthropic’s Claude models. We get them from Anthropic and from cloud providers like Amazon Bedrock and Google Vertex, and if one provider has a problem, we send your request to another. For Claude Code, we recommend setting Anthropic as your first choice of provider, because Claude Code is only guaranteed to work with Anthropic.

blocks.text: Can I use a cheaper model when I hit the limit?

inlines.text: Can I use a cheaper model when I hit the limit?

blocks.text: Yes. Sonnet 5.5 costs about half as much per session as Opus 5.5, and Haiku 5.5 costs less than a cent per session. You can also put a different model in one of the variables in the function. Many people use other models in Claude Code through OpenRouter. This month, GLM 5.3 Flash is the second most used model in Claude Code on our apps page, after Claude Opus 5.5. Claude Code is built for Claude models, though, so try any other model on a small task first. If you call our API from your own code, you can also list fallback models so a request moves to a second model when the first one fails. For more ways to lower what you pay per request, see our guide to the lowest-cost LLM inference on OpenRouter.
